cohort: 776 adult patients undergoing various surgical procedures at a tertiary care hospital in Port Blair, India.
finding: The overall prevalence of surgical site infections (SSIs) was 12.88%, with SSIs occurring more frequently after obstetrics and gynaecology operations and in patients who were women, younger, had emergency surgery, diabetes, and a lengthy hospital stay.
mod_finding: The post-lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) stitch line had the greatest prevalence rate of SSIs (19.42%).
